## The usual way

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Slides in one app, worksheets in another
- Copy the same words into a handout, a website, a packet
- Fix a typo in one place… and miss the other three
- Make a separate version for families and an answer key for you
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-warning title="The result" icon=false}
Five copies of everything, slowly drifting apart. Hours every week spent formatting instead of teaching.
:::
:::
::::

::: notes
Ask the room: how many places does the same lesson live for you right now? Slides, a doc, a shared drive, an LMS page, a printed packet…
:::

## The Chalkline way: one file, many outputs

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
::: {.callout-note title="You write" icon=false}
**One plain-text file** per deck or worksheet: words, pictures, and a few labels at the top (title, type, who it's for).
:::
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
::: {.callout-tip title="Chalkline makes" icon=false}
- **Slides** to present, and a **slide PDF**
- A **web page** and a **printable PDF** of each worksheet
- A **unit packet**: every printable in one PDF, with a cover and contents
- A **year packet** with every unit
- A **student**, a **teacher** and a **family** website
:::
:::
::::

::: notes
Everything in this sample was made this way. Open any slide deck or worksheet file in VS Code to see how little is in it.
:::

## A slide is just text you can read

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
**This is a whole slide.** Open the file and you see:

```{.markdown .friendly-text code-line-numbers="false"}
## Athens and Sparta

- Athens was a democracy.
- Citizens could {{</* vocab "vote" */>}}.
- Sparta trained soldiers.
```

::: {.small-note}
`##` starts a new slide. `-` makes a bullet point. `{{</* vocab "vote" */>}}` adds a vocab pop-up, with 中文 and 🔊. That's most of it.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
::: {style="font-size: 0.82em"}
- ✏️ **Edit it like a document.** Change a word, save, and the slide updates.
- 💬 **Or ask an AI to edit it.** *"Add a bullet about the navy."* Plain text is easy for AI to change correctly.
- 🎨 **It can't look messy.** Fonts, colors and layout come from the school style, on every slide.
- 🔁 **Write once.** The same words become the slides, the web page and the PDF.
:::
:::
::::

```{=html}
<style>
  /* This slide's example reads like plain text, not code: the slide font, bigger, on a soft panel. */
  .reveal div.sourceCode:has(pre.friendly-text), .reveal pre.friendly-text { border: none; background: #ebf7fd; border-radius: 10px; }
  .reveal pre.friendly-text, .reveal pre.friendly-text code { font-family: "Source Sans 3", sans-serif; font-size: 0.95em; line-height: 1.5; color: #1F2933; background: #ebf7fd; }
  .reveal pre.friendly-text code span { color: inherit !important; font-weight: inherit; }
</style>
```

::: notes
For teachers new to this: you don't need to learn a language. Most slides are headings and bullet points, exactly as they look here. When you want something fancier (two columns, a box, a vocab pop-up, a poll), copy it from an existing slide, or ask an AI assistant to add it. Then show the real "Athens and Sparta" slide in Unit 1 to compare.
:::

## Every unit gets a home page

- The unit's **objectives** at the top
- Every slide deck and printable, with links to the PDFs
- A **Unit packet (PDF)** button: all the printables, ready to send to the copier
- Nothing to list by hand: add a file to the unit folder and it appears

::: {.small-note}
Try it: open **Unit 1: Ancient Greece** in the sidebar.
:::

## Packets build themselves

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- Every worksheet, handout and reference in a unit, **in order**
- A **cover** with the objectives and contents
- Page numbers running through the whole packet
- Slides, posters and tests stay out
- Add an **outside PDF** (a map, an official form) with one line
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.callout-note title="Teacher version" icon=false}
The teacher build makes **teacher packets**: the same pages plus answer keys, with an orange **TEACHER EDITION** tab.
:::
:::
::::

::: notes
Packets are made fresh from the source files, not glued together, so they always match the latest worksheets.
:::

## Vocabulary support, built in

Tap or hover a word with a dotted line to see its card: picture, 中文 and a simple definition.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Ancient Athens was a {{< vocab "democracy" >}}.
- Rome built a huge {{< vocab "empire" >}}.
- An {{< vocab "aqueduct" >}} carried water to the city.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-tip title="One list, used everywhere" icon=false}
The words live in one spreadsheet. Slides, worksheets, the **vocab app** and Quizlet/Kahoot exports all read it. **English is the goal; 中文 is support**, and never appears in quizzes.
:::
:::
::::

::: notes
Try the pop-ups now. Then open "History vocab 词汇" in the sidebar: all 37 words from the three units, searchable in English or Chinese.
:::

## Three websites from the same files

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.callout-note title="Students" icon=false}
Slides, worksheets, vocab. No answer keys.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.callout-warning title="Teachers" icon=false}
Everything, plus **answer keys**, **speaker notes** and teacher packets.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.callout-tip title="Families" icon=false}
The objectives, the **vocab app** and only the slides you choose to share.
:::
:::
::::

One label decides who sees a file: `audience: [teacher, student, parent]`

## Classroom tools in every deck

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A **timer** on any slide (press **T**)
- A **clock** in the corner (press **K**)
- **Speaker notes** in a second window (press **S**)
- A **toolbox** (press **W**): scoreboard, voice level, traffic light, noise meter, QR code, stopwatch, dice
- **Tap-to-vote polls**: no devices, no accounts
- **Games**: Snowman, Picture reveal, Jeopardy, Quick-fire (see Unit 1)
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
{{< timer 2 >}}
:::
::::

::: notes
Start the timer to show it. It keeps running in a small box if you change slides.
:::

## Slides can do anything a web page can

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="68%"}
```{=html}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../01-ancient-greece/odyssey/odyssey.css">
<div class="odyssey"></div>
<script src="../01-ancient-greece/odyssey/odyssey.js"></script>
```
:::
::: {.column .ody-side width="32%"}
**The Odyssey 奥德赛:** ten years, ten stops, one hero trying to get home.

Press **Play**, or hover a stop for its story.

::: {.callout-tip title="Made with AI" icon=false}
This map is about 150 lines of code. An AI assistant wrote it from one paragraph: *"Make an interactive map of Odysseus's journey home: numbered stops, a ship that sails the route, and the story of each stop on hover."*

Maps, timelines, games, simulations: if a web page can do it, a slide can too.
:::
:::
::::

::: notes
The code lives in `course/units/01-ancient-greece/odyssey/`, and the Greece unit uses it too. To make your own, describe what you want to an AI assistant (Claude, for example) and ask for a self-contained HTML/JavaScript block for a Quarto reveal.js slide. In the slide PDF the whole route is shown at once.
:::

## It always looks like your school

- Colors, fonts and logos are set **once**, in `brand/`
- Slides, web pages, PDFs and the vocab app all follow
- Change the brand file and **everything** updates

::: {.small-note}
No more fixing fonts slide by slide.
:::

## Editing with an AI assistant

- The files are plain text, so tools like Claude can read and edit them
- `CLAUDE.md` tells the assistant the rules for this course
- While you work on one worksheet, only that file is rebuilt: quick to check
- When it's done: save, and rebuild that unit's packet

::: notes
Example request: "Add a 5-question exit ticket to the Rome republic deck, with Chinese glosses on the key words."
:::

## Get your own copy

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
1. **Install** (once): VS Code, Quarto, Python 3, Git, and Chrome or Edge. The README has the links.
2. **Clone:** in VS Code, press **Ctrl+Shift+P** (Mac: **Cmd+Shift+P**), choose **Git: Clone**, paste the address, pick a folder, then **Open**.
3. **Start:** double-click **Start Chalkline** in the folder. The first time takes a few minutes.
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.callout-tip title="The address" icon=false}
`https://github.com/insufficientdoubt/chalkline-sample`
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Then" icon=false}
Your site opens at **localhost:4100**, in the teacher version. Your copy is yours: change anything.
:::
:::
::::

::: {.small-note}
Just want to look first? The online version: **insufficientdoubt.github.io/chalkline-sample**
:::

::: notes
In a terminal instead of VS Code: `git clone https://github.com/insufficientdoubt/chalkline-sample.git`, then open the folder. No GitHub account is needed to clone; you need one only to save changes back to GitHub.
:::

## How this sample is organized

```{.text code-line-numbers="false"}
course/units/01-ancient-greece/
  index.qmd               the unit page: title, objectives
  city-states-slides.qmd  a slide deck
  athens-vs-sparta.qmd    a worksheet (web + PDF)
  images/                 photos for this unit's slides
vocab/data/vocab.csv      the 37 vocab words
vocab/images/             vocab pictures (GRC-003.svg = democracy)
brand/                    colors, fonts, logos
```

## Make your own unit

1. Copy a unit folder, for example `01-ancient-greece`, and rename it
2. In its `index.qmd`, change the title and objectives
3. Edit or replace the slides and worksheets, keeping a `type:` label on each
4. Add your words to `vocab/data/vocab.csv`
5. Double-click **Start Chalkline**: your unit is on the site
